title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
description: Discover the specific study nooks, quiet gardens, and community hubs that Azusa Pacific University students use to navigate daily life across East and West campuses.

cards.title: The Cougar Dome
cards.subtitle: Student Union Hub on East Campus
cards.notes: Visit the Student Union for free snacks, coffee, and recreational games like ping pong and pool. It serves as a primary lounge for commuter students between classes.
cards.short_summary: A central student union space on East Campus featuring recreational equipment and commuter resources.
cards.evidence_claim: The Cougar Dome is a favorite spot for commuters, offering lounge spaces, free snacks, and games like ping pong and pool.
cards.source_title: APU Students' and Alumni's Favorite Spots On Campus
cards.access_notes: Open Monday–Thursday 8 a.m.-10 p.m. and Friday 8 a.m.-6 p.m. during fall and spring semesters.

cards.title: Mary Hill Garden
cards.subtitle: Quiet Prayer Space on West Campus
cards.notes: Find tranquility at this prayer garden located between the Felix Event Center and Mary Hill Building. It offers views of the flower wall and the prominent campus cross.
cards.short_summary: A peaceful outdoor garden on West Campus designed for prayer and quiet reflection.
cards.evidence_claim: Mary Hill Garden is a peaceful hub for prayer located between the Felix Event Center and the Mary Hill Building on West Campus.
cards.source_title: APU Students' and Alumni's Favorite Spots On Campus
cards.access_notes: Accessible outdoor space on West Campus.

cards.title: Marshburn Library 3rd Floor
cards.subtitle: Study Desks with Sunset Views
cards.notes: Head to the north side windows for views of the amphitheater and local sunsets. This floor is a preferred quiet zone for students tackling heavy workloads.
cards.short_summary: The top floor of Marshburn Library, known for its large windows and quiet study environment.
cards.evidence_claim: Marshburn Library's 3rd floor is noted by students as a perfect place for studying with a view, particularly on the north side by the large windows.
cards.source_title: APU Students' and Alumni's Favorite Spots On Campus
cards.access_notes: Library hours vary by semester; check the official library calendar for current closing times.

cards.title: Segerstrom Atrium
cards.subtitle: Indoor-Outdoor Study Hub
cards.notes: Study near the turtle pond and trees inside this modern science facility. The atrium provides a bright, nature-filled environment for individual or group work.
cards.short_summary: A light-filled atrium in the Segerstrom Science Center featuring natural elements and study seating.
cards.evidence_claim: The Segerstrom Atrium on West Campus is a popular spot for studying and relaxation near the turtle pond and trees.
cards.source_title: APU Students' and Alumni's Favorite Spots On Campus
cards.access_notes: Located within the Segerstrom Science Center on West Campus.

cards.title: Duke Student Commons
cards.subtitle: West Campus Social Space
cards.notes: Gather here for meals or group study sessions. This newer addition to West Campus serves as a secondary living room for students between academic buildings.
cards.short_summary: A modern student commons area on West Campus for dining, socializing, and studying.
cards.evidence_claim: The Duke Student Commons serves as a welcoming space for students to grab a meal, socialize, or find a comfortable place to study.
cards.access_notes: Located within the Duke Academic Complex on West Campus.

cards.title: Stamps Theological Library
cards.subtitle: Quiet Nooks for Deep Focus
cards.notes: Utilize the comfortable couches and quiet corners of this specialized library. It is favored by students seeking a more secluded and focused atmosphere than the main library.
cards.short_summary: A theological library on West Campus offering quiet, cozy study areas and comfortable seating.
cards.evidence_claim: Students use the James L. Stamps Theological Library to find quiet nooks and comfortable couches for focused study.
cards.source_title: APU Students' and Alumni's Favorite Spots On Campus
cards.access_notes: Check library website for specific hours; generally quieter than Marshburn Library.

cards.title: Wynn Amphitheater Turtle Pond
cards.subtitle: Wildlife Observation Spot
cards.notes: Take a break to watch the turtles in the pond located within the Wynn Amphitheater. It is a popular spot for students to decompress between East Campus classes.
cards.short_summary: A small pond located in the Wynn Amphitheater on East Campus, home to resident turtles.
cards.evidence_claim: The turtle pond in Wynn Amphitheater is a favorite spot for students to observe animals and relax.
cards.source_title: APU Students' and Alumni's Favorite Spots On Campus
cards.access_notes: Outdoor amphitheater space on East Campus.

cards.title: Darling Library Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Group Collaboration Spaces
cards.notes: Book a quiet discussion room equipped with TV displays and HDMI ports for group projects. These rooms are located within the Ahmanson Information Center zone.
cards.short_summary: Reservable group study rooms in the Darling Library on West Campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Darling Library offers quiet discussion rooms for 5-8 people that can be booked through the library's LibCal system.
cards.access_notes: Reservations required via LibCal; rooms are for 2-8 people depending on the specific space.

cards.title: Convergent Media Center
cards.subtitle: Student Media Newsroom
cards.notes: Visit the home of ZU Media on West Campus. This facility includes broadcast and podcast studios and serves as a collaborative hub for journalism and PR students.
cards.short_summary: A state-of-the-art newsroom and media production facility for student-run media outlets.
cards.evidence_claim: The Convergent Media Center on West Campus houses ZU Media and provides recording studios and computer stations for student journalists.
cards.source_title: APU's Convergent Media Center Empowers Student Journalists
cards.access_notes: Primarily for student media and communication students; located on West Campus.

cards.title: Dillon Recreation Complex
cards.subtitle: Intramural Sports Field
cards.notes: Join a game of flag football or soccer at this field adjacent to Adams Hall. It is the primary outdoor venue for the university's campus recreation programs.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor athletic field on East Campus used for intramural sports and student recreation.
cards.evidence_claim: The Dillon Recreation Complex is where many flag football and soccer games are played and is adjacent to Adams Hall.
cards.source_title: Campus Recreation Facilities - Azusa Pacific University
cards.access_notes: Open for scheduled intramural sports and general student recreation.
